title: Functional groups
keyIdea: A functional group is the atom or small group of atoms that gives an organic compound its typical reactions. The rest of the molecule is a carbon chain that hardly reacts. Four groups to know: C=C in alkenes, –OH in alcohols, –COOH in carboxylic acids and –COO– in esters. Compounds with the same group react in the same ways, so the group also names the family.

kid: Most of an organic molecule is a chain of carbon atoms with hydrogens around them. That chain is quite dull. It does not react with much.
Stuck on the chain there is often a small special part. We call it the functional group. It is the part that does the reacting.
Alcohols have an O–H on the end, written –OH. Carboxylic acids have –COOH. Alkenes have a double bond, C=C. Esters have –COO– in the middle of the chain.
Here is the trick. If two molecules have the same group, they react in the same way. Ethanol and butanol both fizz with sodium. Their chains are different, but their –OH is the same.
adult: A functional group is the atom or group of atoms responsible for a compound's characteristic reactions. The C–C and C–H bonds of the chain are much less reactive. So every member of a homologous series reacts alike: methanol, propanol and butanol all react with sodium as ethanol does. The group also gives the name ending: -ene, -ol, -oic acid and -oate.

At GCSE there are four groups to spot. Alkenes have C=C and turn bromine water colourless. Alcohols have –OH and give off hydrogen with sodium. Carboxylic acids have –COOH. They are weak acids, so they fizz with carbonates and give carbon dioxide. Esters have –COO– and often smell fruity.

An ester forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol, using an acid catalyst. The acid loses its OH, the alcohol loses the H from its OH, and these leave as water. Ethanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.

Common mistakes: circling only the O of –OH and leaving out its H. Calling a carboxylic acid an alcohol because –COOH contains O–H. Mixing up –COOH with –COO–. Thinking that a longer chain changes which reactions happen.

familyTip: Write a few chain lengths on cards (CH₃, CH₃CH₂, CH₃CH₂CH₂) and the groups on others (–OH, –COOH). Take turns snapping a chain to a group and naming the result, then say one reaction it will have. The reaction depends only on which group card you picked.

worked.title: Name the family of CH₃CH₂COOH and predict one reaction.
steps: Look past the chain. CH₃CH₂ is the same as in ethane and does not react with the usual tests.
The end is COOH: a carbon with a C=O and an O–H on it. Together these are the –COOH group.
–COOH means a carboxylic acid. Three carbons in all, so the name is propanoic acid.
Prediction: like ethanoic acid, it fizzes with sodium carbonate and gives carbon dioxide, because it has the same group.

choices: The atom or group of atoms that gives a compound its typical reactions
The longest carbon chain in the molecule
Any atom that is not carbon
practice.hint: Think about which part of ethanol reacts with sodium.
practice.explain: The functional group, such as –OH, decides how a compound reacts. The chain hardly reacts, and hydrogen is not carbon but is not a group on its own.

practice.prompt: An alcohol has {n} carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does it have in total, counting the one in –OH?
practice.hint: Alcohols fit CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. Add the H in the chain to the H in –OH.
practice.explain: The chain has 2 × {n} + 1 = {=2*n+1} H and the –OH adds 1, so {=2*n+2} in total.

practice.prompt: A carboxylic acid has {n} carbon atoms, counting the carbon in –COOH. How many hydrogen atoms does it have?
practice.hint: Methanoic acid is HCOOH and ethanoic acid is CH₃COOH. Each extra carbon adds CH₂.
practice.explain: Carboxylic acids fit CₙH₂ₙO₂, so {n} carbons carry 2 × {n} = {=2*n} hydrogens.

choices: –COOH, so it is a carboxylic acid
C=C, so it is an alkene
practice.hint: Read the end of the formula. Is there a C=O next to the OH?
practice.explain: The OH is on a plain CH₂ with no C=O, so the group is –OH. This is propanol, an alcohol.

practice.prompt: Which test result shows a compound has a –COOH group?
practice.hint: Carboxylic acids are acids. What do acids do with carbonates?
practice.explain: Acids release carbon dioxide from carbonates. Clearing bromine water is the C=C test, and a fruity smell suggests an ester.

pool.prompt: Which part of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is its functional group?
pool.hint: The OH sits on a carbon that also has a C=O. Do they work alone?
pool.explain: The C=O and the O–H on the same carbon act together as –COOH. CH₃ is part of the chain.

pool.prompt: CH₃COOCH₃ is shown. Which family is it in?
pool.hint: Look at what is on the far side of the single-bonded O: an H or a carbon?
pool.explain: A carbon is on the far side of that O, so the group is –COO–. That makes it an ester, methyl ethanoate.

pool.prompt: Ethanol reacts with sodium. Why can you predict that butanol will too?
pool.hint: Which part of the molecule does the reacting?
pool.explain: The –OH group reacts with sodium. Butanol has the same group, so it reacts the same way; the longer chain does not change that.

pool.prompt: A hydrocarbon turns bromine water from orange to colourless. Which group does it have?
pool.hint: Bromine adds across one kind of bond.
pool.explain: Bromine adds across a C=C double bond, which removes the orange colour. A hydrocarbon cannot have –OH or –COOH, which contain oxygen.

pool.prompt: An ester is made from ethanoic acid and an alcohol with {n} carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms does the ester have?
pool.hint: All the carbons of the acid and the alcohol end up in the ester. Only water leaves.
pool.explain: Water takes no carbon, so the ester keeps 2 from ethanoic acid plus {n} from the alcohol: {=n+2}.

pool.prompt: Sam says CH₃COOH is an alcohol because it contains O–H. What is wrong?
choices: The O–H is part of –COOH, so it is a carboxylic acid
It has no oxygen at all
pool.hint: Look at the carbon the O–H is joined to. What else is on it?
pool.explain: That carbon also has a C=O, so the atoms form –COOH. Carboxylic acids react with carbonates, which alcohols do not.

pool.prompt: What leaves when ethanol and ethanoic acid join to form an ester?
pool.hint: The acid loses OH and the alcohol loses an H. Put them together.
pool.explain: OH + H makes H₂O. The rest joins up as ethyl ethanoate with a –COO– group.

pool.prompt: Which pair of compounds will react in the same ways?
pool.hint: Same reactions need the same functional group, not the same number of carbons.
pool.explain: Propanol and pentanol both have –OH. Propane has no group, and propanoic acid has –COOH, so they react differently.

pool.prompt: An ester is made from methanol and a carboxylic acid with {n} carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms does the ester have?
pool.hint: Count the H in the acid and in methanol, then take away the two H atoms that leave in water.
pool.explain: The acid has 2 × {n} = {=2*n} H and methanol has 4. Water takes 2, leaving {=2*n} + 4 − 2 = {=2*n+2}.

visual.caption: Which family? Find the functional group, then drag each formula to its family, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: circle the functional group, test molecules with bromine water, sodium and sodium carbonate, then make an ester.
